# ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  AUDIT MARKER REGISTRY — must-be-present tokens                          ║
# ╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
# ║                                                                          ║
# ║  Each non-blank, non-comment line is a marker token that MUST appear at  ║
# ║  least once somewhere in the tracked source tree (excluding              ║
# ║  node_modules, .next, dist, build, public). The audit-marker-guard CI    ║
# ║  workflow fails any push or PR where a registered marker has gone        ║
# ║  missing, blocking accidental regression.                                ║
# ║                                                                          ║
# ║  WHY THIS EXISTS:                                                        ║
# ║  Multiple agents work on this codebase in parallel. Without a guard, a   ║
# ║  PR built from a stale local copy can silently revert another PR's       ║
# ║  fixes when it lands on main (observed: commit 2ac380fe wiped LV-AUDIT   ║
# ║  fixes from PRs #257/#258/#259 with +17/-115 lines on lives.js, all     ║
# ║  while passing review). This registry + the CI workflow make such a    ║
# ║  regression FAIL THE BUILD instead of silently shipping.                ║
# ║                                                                          ║
# ║  TO RETIRE A MARKER (intentional removal):                              ║
# ║  Delete its line from this file in the SAME PR that removes the marker  ║
# ║  from code. The CI workflow only scans the registered tokens, so an    ║
# ║  explicit registry edit is required to land any removal.                ║
# ║                                                                          ║
# ║  TO ADD A NEW MARKER (when shipping a new audit fix):                   ║
# ║  Add the token here in the same PR as the new fix. Use a short          ║
# ║  hyphen-delimited tag (LV-AUDIT-N, EC-N, GLM-N, etc.) and embed it as   ║
# ║  a comment near the affected code, e.g.                                 ║
# ║    // BUG FIX (LV-AUDIT-12): explanation of what was wrong              ║
# ║                                                                          ║
# ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

# ─── pages/hub/user/[username].js — profile lookup hardening ────────────────
# USER-LOOKUP-1 — fixes 'User Not Found' when clicking profile avatars even
# though the profile exists. Root cause: select('*') triggers a 403 from
# PostgREST because phone+email columns have column-level REVOKE.
# See src/lib/profileColumns.js header and /hub/user/[username].js comment.
USER-LOOKUP-1

# ─── pages/hub/user/[username].js — post delete + mobile layout ─────────────
# USER-DELETE-1 — handleDeletePost was fire-and-forget on the DB delete and
# fired same-tab cache invalidation BEFORE the DB write completed, causing
# the optimistic-removed post to be re-fetched and re-added to state. User
# had to click delete a second time. Fix: await the DB delete THEN broadcast.
USER-DELETE-1
# USER-DELETE-2 — social_reels.source_post_id FK was ON DELETE SET NULL, so
# deleting a profile post left an orphan reel that kept playing in /hub/reels.
# App-layer defense in depth: explicitly delete matching reels after post
# delete confirms. Backed by a DB migration changing FK to ON DELETE CASCADE.
USER-DELETE-2
# USER-LAYOUT-1 — explicit width / max-width / box-sizing on the .sp-profile-page
# wrapper to prevent the page from rendering in a narrow column on mobile when
# an ancestor has a stale width / flex-basis. Reported visible after the
# USER-LOOKUP-1 fix made the page actually render.
USER-LAYOUT-1

# ─── pages/hub/reels.js — DELETE realtime subscriptions ─────────────────────
# REELS-DELETE-1 — subscribe to DELETE events on social_reels so deleted reels
# disappear from /hub/reels in real time instead of continuing to play.
REELS-DELETE-1
# REELS-DELETE-2 — also subscribe to DELETE on social_posts and filter reels
# whose source_post_id matches; covers the case where a profile post-delete
# transitively means the reel should disappear.
REELS-DELETE-2


# ─── /hub/training — Surface C (post-answer feedback) critical bugs ─────────
# TRAIN-RANGE-PCT-1 — RangeGrid.jsx rangeStats useMemo. The previous formula
# assumed gridData[hand][action] was already 0–100 percent, but UDT and other
# callers sometimes pass freqs in a different unit (raw 0–1 fractions, basis
# points ×10, or pre-summed across solver subtrees). That caused per-hand
# `combos` to far exceed `weight`, and grand totals to exceed totalCombos
# (1326), printing impossible filter-pill percentages such as Fold 35693.8%
# and (18472/1326 combos). Fix: per-hand normalize so each cell's actions
# sum to ≤100 before applying weight, mathematically guaranteeing
# actionTotals ≤ totalCombos regardless of input scale.
TRAIN-RANGE-PCT-1
# TRAIN-ACTIONS-COUNT-1 — UniversalDynamicTable.jsx displayOptions useMemo.
# Question pipeline sometimes pre-trims `options` to 2 entries on a postflop
# spot where ≥4 actions should be available. After groupActions returns, top
# up displayOptions from `options` then computedFrequencies (highest-frequency
# missing actions first) until length ≥ 4 in standard difficulty mode. Push/
# fold short-stack trainers are detected via the {push, fold, allin} ID set
# and left at 2 buttons.
TRAIN-ACTIONS-COUNT-1
# TRAIN-ERROR-BOUNDARY-1 — GlobalErrorCatcher.jsx. Logged uncaught errors and
# unhandled rejections at console.warn level, which is invisible in many
# production log filters and silently swallowed state-corruption errors that
# the training surface was throwing. Tightened to console.error on both code
# paths, and the dev-mode toast now names the underlying error type and a
# trimmed message so triage is actionable. Production toast text unchanged.
TRAIN-ERROR-BOUNDARY-1

# ─── /hub/training — Bug 2B follow-up (deferred from PR1) ───────────────────
# TRAIN-FEEDBACK-SYNC-1 — UniversalDynamicTable.jsx defensive guard against
# the templated explanation / structured-explanation / solver-line narrative
# referencing a board, hand, or position different from the scenario being
# rendered on the active table. Symptom: table shows K8 on AT5 but feedback
# says "On the Qc Kc 7d flop, you hold 86o from the CO." Root cause is in
# the scenario pipeline (tracked as #283); this guard prevents wrong text
# from reaching users while the upstream fix is built.
TRAIN-FEEDBACK-SYNC-1

# ─── /hub/training — Surface B (active table) layout polish ─────────────────
# TRAIN-LAYOUT-QUIT-1 — UniversalDynamicTable.jsx Quit button. Was absolutely
# positioned at top:-40, left:0 relative to the action bar. The Hint ribbon
# rendered in the flow immediately above the action bar, so Quit visibly
# overlapped the hint text. Lifted Quit out of the action-bar layer and
# pinned it to the viewport's top-left corner with iOS/Android safe-area
# awareness so it cannot collide with any bottom-UI element.
TRAIN-LAYOUT-QUIT-1

# ─── /hub/training — Surface C (post-answer feedback) IA pass ───────────────
# TRAIN-FB-COPY-1 — UniversalDynamicTable.jsx Hand Summary header. The previous
# wording "Hand Complete — 1 STREET PLAYED" reads awkwardly on mobile and is
# both ambiguous (which street?) and SCREAMING-CAPS. Replaced with a natural
# language map: 1 → "Played to flop", 2 → "Played to turn", 3 → "Played to
# river", 4 → "Hand to showdown", and a generic fallback for higher counts.
TRAIN-FB-COPY-1
# TRAIN-FB-IA-1 — UniversalDynamicTable.jsx auxiliary feedback cards. The
# post-answer feedback layer was stacking up to 10 narrative cards (PRINCIPLE
# / POSITION / TEXTURE / SPR / VILLAIN RANGE / STREET PLAN / HAND / EQUITY /
# RANGE TIP / HAND READING) on top of the KEY TAKEAWAY and SOLVER LINE cards.
# On a 390px mobile viewport this filled the screen and pushed the NEXT HAND
# button below the fold. Wrapped them in a single <details> accordion ("More
# coaching insights") so the two important cards stay visible by default and
# the deep insights are opt-in.
TRAIN-FB-IA-1

# ─── /hub/training — cross-cutting CSS sweep across all 89 game pages ───────
# TRAIN-CSS-SWEEP-1 — src/styles/worlds/training.css. The training theme file
# was 1.3KB of theme variables only; zero accessibility, responsive, or motion
# rules. Added 9 cross-cutting rule blocks at body.world-training scope so
# every training route inherits them without per-page edits:
#   1. No horizontal scroll on mobile (lock body overflow-x)
#   2. WCAG 2.5.5 — touch target min 44×44 on mobile
#   3. :focus-visible rings for keyboard accessibility
#   4. prefers-reduced-motion respect (force ~0ms animations when set)
#   5. Safe-area awareness for fixed elements via [data-safe-*] hooks
#   6. No-FOUC dark backdrop
#   7. Tap-delay killer (touch-action: manipulation)
#   8. .sr-only utility for icon-only-button labels
#   9. Themed scrollbars
#  10. Print stylesheet for sane Cmd-P output
# Each block addresses a specific anti-pattern category from the May 8
# training-overhaul handoff and the ui-ux-pro-max design-system standards.
TRAIN-CSS-SWEEP-1

# ─── /hub/training — typography rhythm + spacing scale (sweep #2) ───────────
# TRAIN-CSS-TYPO-1 — src/styles/worlds/training.css second sweep block.
# Companion to TRAIN-CSS-SWEEP-1 which added a11y/responsive guards. This
# block adds an additive utility layer scoped to body.world-training so
# pages can adopt sp-* classes for consistent vertical rhythm and spacing
# without breaking existing inline-style layouts:
#   1. Semantic heading sizes (sp-h1..h4) — modular scale anchored at 16px
#   2. Body text utilities (sp-body, sp-body-sm, sp-caption) with line-height 1.5+
#   3. Tabular numerals (sp-num-tabular) for data displays
#   4. Spacing scale (sp-stack-1..7, sp-cluster-1..6) on 4/8/12/16/24/32/48 increments
#   5. Card padding tokens (sp-card / -sm / -lg)
#   6. CTA button base (sp-cta + -primary / -secondary / -ghost variants)
#   7. Truncation helpers (sp-truncate, sp-truncate-2, sp-truncate-3)
#   8. Section dividers (sp-divider)
#   9. Empty-state pattern (sp-empty, sp-empty-title)
#  10. Skeleton shimmer (sp-skeleton, sp-skeleton-line, sp-skeleton-block) —
#      honors prefers-reduced-motion via the guard from TRAIN-CSS-SWEEP-1.
TRAIN-CSS-TYPO-1

# ─── /hub/training — ConnectionToast emoji→SVG (46 pages) ───────────────────
# TRAIN-TOAST-SVG-1 — src/components/training/ConnectionToast.js. Replaced
# emoji icons (lightning bolt and check) with inline Lucide-style SVG. The
# May 8 handoff §4 lists 'no-emoji-icons — Use SVG icons (Heroicons, Lucide),
# not emojis' as an explicit anti-pattern; emojis are font-dependent, render
# inconsistently across platforms, cannot be controlled via design tokens,
# and don't tint with currentColor. Also tightened aria-live to 'assertive'
# when offline (interruption the screen reader should announce immediately)
# vs 'polite' when reconnected (reassurance, can wait). 46 training pages
# import this component, so the fix propagates broadly. Adds a
# prefers-reduced-motion guard for the slideUp animation.
TRAIN-TOAST-SVG-1

# ─── /hub/training — ErrorBanner polish (28 pages) ──────────────────────────
# TRAIN-ERROR-BANNER-1 — src/components/training/ErrorBanner.js polishing
# pass on the shared error UI used by 28 training pages.
#   1. Body text bumped from 12px to 14px (handoff §6 readability floor;
#      12px under-reads on dense training pages).
#   2. Added leading alert-triangle SVG (Lucide-style) for visual hierarchy
#      — handoff §8 'error-recovery' wants errors distinct from regular
#      content; an icon establishes the affordance.
#   3. aria-atomic="true" on the alert role so screen readers re-announce
#      the FULL banner when message changes, not just the diff.
#   4. Retry button uses :focus-visible offset and minimum 32px height for
#      better keyboard + touch ergonomics.
TRAIN-ERROR-BANNER-1

# ─── /hub/training — PageTransition reduced-motion + dvh (14 pages) ─────────
# TRAIN-PAGE-TRANSITION-1 — src/components/transitions/PageTransition.jsx.
# Two issues: (1) framer-motion uses JS transforms not CSS animations, so the
# CSS-level prefers-reduced-motion guard from TRAIN-CSS-SWEEP-1 doesn't catch
# it — users who set Reduce Motion at the OS level still saw slide+scale on
# every page transition. Fix: read framer-motion's useReducedMotion() hook
# and switch to a cross-fade only when reduced-motion is requested. (2)
# minHeight: '100vh' is the handoff §5 viewport-units anti-pattern; 100vh on
# mobile includes the address-bar area and causes scroll/jank. Replaced with
# 100dvh (Chrome 108+, Safari 15.4+, Firefox 101+).
TRAIN-PAGE-TRANSITION-1

# ─── /hub/training — backend RPCs for dashboard surfaces ────────────────────
# TRAIN-DB-DASHBOARD-1 — supabase/migrations/20260510175000_training_dashboard_rpcs.sql.
# The May 8 handoff claimed these RPCs were already applied via an earlier
# migration (20260507120000_training_dashboard_rpcs.sql) but a SELECT against
# pg_proc on 2026-05-10 confirmed that NO `training_*` functions existed in
# production. This migration creates them and grants EXECUTE to the
# `authenticated` role only. Functions:
#   - training_dashboard_30day_stats(uuid, text)
#   - training_dashboard_last_session(uuid, text)
#   - training_dashboard_lifetime_stats(uuid, text)
# Each function is SECURITY DEFINER but checks auth.uid() = p_user_id at the
# top so callers can only see their own stats. Migration applied to
# production via Supabase MCP apply_migration on 2026-05-10 and verified via
# pg_proc on the same date. Unblocks the deferred Session Setup popup
# (issue #288) which needs these stats for the YOUR PERFORMANCE (30 DAYS) card.
TRAIN-DB-DASHBOARD-1

# TRAIN-SETUP-MODAL-1 — src/components/training/SessionSetupModal.jsx (new

# tile click and the GodModeArena render. Surfaces session goal + 30-day
# stats + difficulty/timer/training-mode pills + Start Training CTA per
# the May 8 training-overhaul handoff (issue #288).
#
# Data sources:
#   - training_dashboard_30day_stats RPC (TRAIN-DB-DASHBOARD-1)
#   - training_dashboard_last_session RPC (TRAIN-DB-DASHBOARD-1)
# Persistence: localStorage `sp-train-prefs-${gameId}` remembers last
# difficulty / timer / mode pick.
# Styling: uses sp-* utility classes from TRAIN-CSS-SWEEP-1 and
# TRAIN-CSS-TYPO-1 so it inherits a11y + touch + reduced-motion guards.

TRAIN-SETUP-MODAL-1

# ─── /hub/training — header chip consolidation (PR4 follow-up) ──────────────
# TRAIN-HEADER-CHIPS-1 — src/components/training/games/UniversalDynamicTable.jsx
# RNG and TRAIN/STUDY chips. The May 8 training-overhaul handoff §2E
# specifically called out: "fold related ones (SOLVER+FULL into one mode
# chip; RNG OFF + TRAIN into one)". Consolidated the RNG + TRAIN/STUDY pair
# into a single segmented pill: outer rounded container + two flush-joined
# inner buttons with a shared center divider. Reads as one "session mode"
# control instead of two competing chips. Both inner buttons carry
# data-compact so the global mobile 44px touch-target rule from
# TRAIN-CSS-SWEEP-1 leaves them at their intentionally compact size.
# aria-pressed states + title tooltips added.
TRAIN-HEADER-CHIPS-1

# ─── /hub/training — sticky NEXT HAND button on mobile (PR2 follow-up) ──────
# TRAIN-NEXT-HAND-STICKY-1 — src/components/training/games/UniversalDynamicTable.jsx
# Next Hand / Continue Hand button row. When the feedback panel is long
# (10+ auxiliary insight cards even after the TRAIN-FB-IA-1 accordion
# collapse), the primary CTA used to fall below the fold on mobile, forcing
# users to scroll back down after each answer. Wrapped the button row in
# position:sticky bottom anchor with env(safe-area-inset-bottom) awareness
# and a subtle gradient fade so the button stays visible as soon as the
# feedback panel exceeds the viewport height. Desktop behaviour is unchanged
# because position:sticky has no effect until content scrolls past the
# button's natural inline position.
TRAIN-NEXT-HAND-STICKY-1

# ─── /hub/training — frontend race root-cause fix (closes #283) ─────────────
# TRAIN-FEEDBACK-SNAPSHOT-1 — src/components/training/games/UniversalDynamicTable.jsx.
# Companion to TRAIN-FEEDBACK-SYNC-1 (PR #286) which added a defensive
# explanationMatchesScenario() guard that suppressed wrong feedback text.
# This sweep targets the underlying race: when the parent (Director.tsx /
# GameSession.tsx) eagerly preloads the NEXT question while feedback is
# still on screen, the live `question` prop changes under the feedback
# render path, so the guard's "matches" check uses the NEW scenario and
# can either pass through stale text or suppress correct text.
#
# Fix: route feedback-render guards through a new getFeedbackQuestion()
# accessor that returns lastQuestionRef.current (snapshotted while
# !showFeedback) during the feedback window, and the live prop otherwise.
# All three TRAIN-FEEDBACK-SYNC-1 guard sites updated: displayExplanation
# construction (~3954), structuredExplanation.takeaway (~4234), and the
# Phase 301 SOLVER LINE narration (~4458). Closes issue #283.
TRAIN-FEEDBACK-SNAPSHOT-1

# ─── /hub/training/skill-tree — visible surface a11y + emoji→SVG ────────────
# TRAIN-SKILL-TREE-A11Y-1 — pages/hub/training/skill-tree.js. The 12-level
# progression map (FOUNDATIONS → BOSS MODE per the May 8 handoff) had four
# emoji branch icons (🃏 🎯 ⚡ 👑), three emoji node-status icons (🔒 ✅ 🎯),
# and an emoji back-arrow (←) — all anti-patterns per handoff §4 'no-emoji-
# icons'. Plus no semantic heading levels and no aria-labels on the back
# button or the XP status chip. Replacements:
#   - New BranchIcon component renders Lucide-style SVGs based on branch.id
#     (preflop / postflop / advanced / mastery), uses currentColor.
#   - Node status: SVG lock / check / target circle conditional on state.
#   - Back button: SVG arrow + aria-label="Back to training".
#   - Page title becomes semantic h1; branch headers become semantic h2.
#   - XP chip gets role="status" + aria-label and tabular numerals.
# Visible surface, no other touches.
TRAIN-SKILL-TREE-A11Y-1

# ─── /hub/training/daily-challenge — surface a11y polish ─────────────────────
# TRAIN-DAILY-CHALLENGE-A11Y-1 — pages/hub/training/daily-challenge.js. The
# daily-challenge page surface had four anti-patterns vs the May 8 visible-
# surface a11y guidance (handoff §4): (1) back button used only an HTML
# entity '&larr;' for label, no aria-label, no explicit type, so screen
# readers spoke "Training" alone with no semantic context for the icon;
# (2) inline retry button on the load-error banner had no aria-label or
# type, presenting as a context-free "Retry"; (3) share-result button
# (post-answer flow) had no aria-label or type; (4) "About Daily Challenge"
# section used a styled <div> instead of a semantic heading, breaking the
# h1→h2 outline for screen-reader navigation. Patch: explicit type="button"
# + aria-label on all three buttons, and lift the About section to <h2>
# while preserving its original inline style chrome. Visible surface only,
# no logic changes.
TRAIN-DAILY-CHALLENGE-A11Y-1

# ─── /hub/training/achievements — surface a11y + emoji→SVG ──────────────────
# TRAIN-ACHIEVEMENTS-A11Y-1 — pages/hub/training/achievements.js. The training
# achievements page surface had seven emoji icons (🏅 header, 🎯 🔥 📚 👑
# category map, 🏆 ach-card fallback, ✓ unlocked marker) and an unlabeled
# share button. Replacements: new MedalIcon (header), CategoryIcon (renders

# CheckIcon (unlocked). Share button gets type="button" + per-achievement
# aria-label '"Share '${ach.name}' achievement to your feed"'. Stat counters
# gain role="status" so screen readers announce updates after SESSION_END
# refetch. Skeleton wrapper gets role="status" + aria-label. Progress bars

# role="tablist". Same surface-specific pattern as PR #320/#322/#324/#327.
TRAIN-ACHIEVEMENTS-A11Y-1

# ─── /hub/training/training-feed — surface a11y + emoji→SVG ─────────────────
# TRAIN-FEED-A11Y-1 — pages/hub/training/training-feed.js. Social activity

# ─── Shared PlayingCard component — canonical 52-deck PNG everywhere ────────
# TRAIN-PLAYCARD-1 — src/components/poker/PlayingCard.jsx (new). Shared
# React component that renders any single playing card using the canonical
# custom 52-deck PNG asset set at /public/cards/{suit}_{rank}.png (same
# deck used by Club Arena, sandbox, hand-replayer). Accepts shorthand
# strings ('As', '10h'), explicit rank+suit, or engine cardId 0-51.
# Five size presets (xs 24px / sm 36px / md 60px / lg 90px / xl 120px),
# faceDown + cardBack support, highlighted + dimmed states, onClick with
# role=button + keyboard handler, aria-label derived from full card name.
# Aspect ratio locked at 150:210. Build-safe: no emoji chars (suit glyph
# parsing uses \u escapes), no JSX comments in conditional expressions.
# This unblocks subsequent PRs that replace inline unicode-string card
# rendering across all 89 training surfaces with the shared component.
TRAIN-PLAYCARD-1

# TRAIN-BOTTOMSHEET-1 — src/components/ui/BottomSheet.jsx (new). Controlled
# mobile bottom-sheet (also supports placement=right for desktop side rail).
# Backdrop-click + Escape close. Focus trap + body scroll lock while open.
# Drag-handle visual + safe-area-inset-bottom padding. Slide-up / slide-left
# keyframes with prefers-reduced-motion collapse. Build-safe: no emoji
# chars, no JSX comments in conditional expressions.
TRAIN-BOTTOMSHEET-1

# ─── Shared useTrainingFeedback hook — sound + haptics ──────────────────────
# TRAIN-FEEDBACK-FX-1 — src/hooks/useTrainingFeedback.js (new). Unified
# audio + vibration feedback for trainer surfaces, both gated by per-user
# localStorage preferences (sp.training.sound, sp.training.haptics) and
# globally respecting prefers-reduced-motion (skip vibration + halve
# audio gain). Five primitives: correct (C-E-G chord), incorrect (low G3
# buzz), click (A5 tick), complete (C-E-G-C arpeggio), warning (E4 double
# pulse). WebAudio synthesis means zero asset loads + no autoplay-policy
# issues. iOS Safari has no Vibration API — silent no-op. Build-safe.
TRAIN-FEEDBACK-FX-1

# ─── SQL data improvements — rollup table + leaderboard MV + replay table ───
# TRAIN-DATA-ROLLUPS-1 — supabase/migrations/20260511180000_training_rollups.sql
# Three deliverables: training_user_progress rollup (PK user_id, updated by
# AFTER INSERT trigger on jarvis_training_sessions, generated accuracy
# column), training_leaderboard_top materialized view (top-500, ROW_NUMBER
# rank, refreshable via training_leaderboard_refresh() SECURITY DEFINER
# RPC), training_hand_replay table (per-hand replay events with
# user_id/question_id/board_cards/actions JSONB) + training_hand_replay_
# recent(p_limit) RPC. RLS self-read/insert/delete on both new tables.
# Backfill from existing jarvis_training_sessions in-place.
# Migration file checked in because the live Supabase MCP connection timed
# out — apply via supabase db push or psql -f.
TRAIN-DATA-ROLLUPS-1

# ─── First adoption: wire shared PlayingCard into bluff-catcher ─────────────
# TRAIN-WIRE-PLAYCARD-1 — pages/hub/training/bluff-catcher.js. Replaces the
# inline unicode-string card rendering (e.g. {scenario.board} as a single
# styled <div>'A♠ K♦ 7♣ 4♥ 2♠') with a row of <PlayingCard /> components.
# Board cards use size=md priority. Hero cards use size=md highlighted
# priority. Demonstrates the adoption pattern for the remaining trainers.
# Build-safe: no JSX comments inside conditionals, the existing SCENARIOS
# data still contains card-suit glyphs (♠♣♦♥) in string literals which is
# the same form that was on main pre-patch.
TRAIN-WIRE-PLAYCARD-1

# ─── Phase-9 adoption: UDT migrates action bar to shared ActionButton ───────
# TRAIN-WIRE-UDT-ACTIONBTN-1 — src/components/training/games/UniversalDynamic
# Table.jsx + src/components/poker/ActionButton.jsx (v1.1.0). ActionButton
# extended with slot props: topLeftSlot, topRightSlot, children, footerSlot,
# shortcutPosition, and two new size presets (compact, veryCompact) matching
# UDT's existing responsive sizing math. UDT's displayOptions.map(option)
# motion.button render replaced with <ActionButton> that:
#   * uses size = veryCompact | compact | md based on optionCount
#   * passes UDT's existing shortcut badge JSX as topLeftSlot (preserves
#     exact pixel-level styling)
#   * passes per-action EV chip JSX as topRightSlot
#   * passes BB-sizing sublabel + frequency label motion.span as children
#   * keeps FrequencyBar as a sibling AFTER the ActionButton (not via
#     footerSlot, since UDT's existing wrapper div pattern is preserved)
#   * inherits getActionButtonStyle's bespoke per-option colors via the
#     style prop
# whileHover/whileTap framer-motion mics are replaced by ActionButton's
# onMouseDown translateY(1px) microinteraction; functionally equivalent.
# This closes the deferred Task #88 epic that required widening
# ActionButton's prop surface before UDT migration was safe.
TRAIN-WIRE-UDT-ACTIONBTN-1

# ─── Phase-14 infrastructure: semantic --sp-* token contract ────────────────
# TRAIN-CSS-TOKENS-1 — src/styles/worlds/training.css. Adds a complete

# triplets + neutral ramp + surface ramp + verdict semantic aliases).

# tracked separately by TRAIN-CSS-TOKENS-ADOPT-* markers as files migrate.
TRAIN-CSS-TOKENS-1

# ─── Phase-15a adoption: --sp-* token adoption in trainers ──────────────────
# TRAIN-CSS-TOKENS-ADOPT-1 — pages/hub/training/bluff-catcher.js. Replaces
# 17 quoted hex literals with var(--sp-*) tokens from PR #470's contract:
#   '#00d4ff' (x6)  -> var(--sp-accent-cyan)
#   '#94a3b8' (x4)  -> var(--sp-fg-muted)
#   '#ef4444' (x2)  -> var(--sp-accent-red)
#   '#4ade80' (x1)  -> var(--sp-accent-green)
#   '#cbd5e1' (x1)  -> var(--sp-fg)
#   '#e2e8f0' (x1)  -> var(--sp-fg)
#   '#fbbf24' (x1)  -> var(--sp-accent-amber)
#   '#f97316' (x1)  -> var(--sp-accent-orange)
# Page-bg darks (#05050a, #0a0a15) preserved — outside the accent contract.
# String-interpolation contexts (e.g. `${color}33` hex-alpha suffix) left for

# ─── Phase-SQL audit: training_sessions UPDATE/DELETE RLS ───────────────────
# TRAIN-SQL-RLS-1 — supabase/migrations/20260512100000_training_sessions_owner_update_delete_rls.sql.
# Closes the UPDATE/DELETE RLS gap on public.training_sessions. Pre-state: the
# table had only INSERT + SELECT policies; UPDATE/DELETE from the frontend
# silently no-opped. Migration adds two owner-scoped policies that pin the
# subject to (SELECT auth.uid()) = user_id. The existing SECURITY DEFINER
# rollup trigger tup_after_session_delete continues to revert tup totals on
# legitimate self-deletes.
TRAIN-SQL-RLS-1

# ─── Phase-18 infrastructure: semantic motion tokens ────────────────────────
# TRAIN-CSS-MOTION-1 — src/styles/worlds/training.css. Adds a complete
# motion-token contract on body.world-training: duration ramp
# (--sp-motion-instant/fast/standard/slow/glacial) plus easing curve presets
# (--sp-ease-standard/in/out/in-out/spring-soft/spring-snap). A second
# @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block collapses the duration
# tokens to 0.01ms so any code that reads them is reduced-motion-safe by
# construction. Belt-and-braces with the existing TRAIN-CSS-SWEEP-1
# blanket override above. Adoption tracked separately under
# TRAIN-CSS-MOTION-ADOPT-* markers.
TRAIN-CSS-MOTION-1

# ─── Phase-32: useTriviaQuestion hook ───────────────────────────────────────
# TRAIN-TRIVIA-HOOK-1 — src/hooks/useTriviaQuestion.js. New shared hook
# encapsulating the selectedAnswer / showResult / isCorrect / selectAnswer /
# reset state plumbing duplicated across 5 trivia mode files. Adopters
# call useTriviaQuestion(currentQuestion, {onAnswer}) and skip ~25 lines
# of state boilerplate per file. Hook also adds an internal lockedRef to
# prevent the double-fire race that several trivia pages hand-rolled with
# different inline guards. Adoption can land incrementally.
TRAIN-TRIVIA-HOOK-1


# ─── Phase-33/34/35: useTriviaQuestion hook adoption (3 CSS-class adopters) ──
# TRAIN-WIRE-TRIVIA-HOOK-1 — pages/hub/trivia/mixed.js. First adopter of
# useTriviaQuestion. Replaces the inline useState plumbing (selectedAnswer +
# showResult) and the hand-rolled function selectAnswer(index) with the
# shared hook. Mode-specific side effects (timer stop, per-category stats,
# scoring, answersRef ledger, busEmit, 1200ms advance via setTimeout)
# live in the hook's onAnswer callback so external semantics are identical.
TRAIN-WIRE-TRIVIA-HOOK-1
# TRAIN-WIRE-TRIVIA-HOOK-2 — pages/hub/trivia/pvp.js. Second hook adopter.
# Same pattern as HOOK-1 but with PvP-specific side effects (per-question
# accuracy ledger via playerAnswersRef, scoreRef, 500ms advance). PR #504
# also restored the missing TriviaAnswerOption import that PR #497 had
# left dangling — would have crashed the PvP playing screen at runtime.
TRAIN-WIRE-TRIVIA-HOOK-2
# TRAIN-WIRE-TRIVIA-HOOK-3 — pages/hub/trivia/tournaments.js. Third hook
# adopter. Same pattern with tournament-specific side effects (scoreRef
# += 100 per correct, answersRef ledger, finishRoundPlay on last question,
# 500ms advance). PR #505 also restored the missing TriviaAnswerOption
# import (same latent crash as pvp.js had).
TRAIN-WIRE-TRIVIA-HOOK-3
